does: Prepares yogurt so that it can be heated and simmered without splitting into curds and thin liquid. A starch or a beaten egg white is mixed into the cold yogurt, and the yogurt is stirred one way as it heats.

intro.what: This yogurt method mixes in starch or egg white before gentle heating.
intro.why: It teaches you to protect a smooth texture by preparing the mixture and controlling heat.

how: Whisk the yogurt smooth in a pan, off the heat.
Mix a little cornstarch with cold water until smooth, or beat an egg white loose, and whisk it into the yogurt.
Set the pan over a low heat and stir all the time, always in the same direction.
Bring it slowly up to a bare simmer without letting it boil hard, and keep stirring until it is thick and smooth.
Keep it at a gentle simmer from then on.

cues.text: The yogurt stays smooth and creamy, with no grains and no pool of thin liquid at the sides.
The spoon meets a gentle, even drag, like a thick cream.

mistakes.mistake: Heating plain yogurt fast, or stirring it first one way and then the other, so that it breaks into curds.
mistakes.fix: Stabilise it first and stir in one direction only.

mistakes.mistake: Letting the stabilised yogurt boil hard, which can still break it.
mistakes.fix: Hold it at a gentle simmer.

quiz.question: What does stabilising yogurt aim to prevent?
choices: Separation into curds and thin liquid during heating.
quiz.because: The added stabiliser and gentle heat help maintain a smooth creamy mixture.

quiz.question: When is the stabiliser mixed into the yogurt?
choices: After the yogurt has boiled hard and separated.
While the yogurt is cold and off the heat.
Only after serving the hot sauce.
quiz.because: Mixing before heating distributes the stabiliser through the yogurt in advance.

quiz.question: Which appearance suggests a smooth heated yogurt sauce?
choices: Small curds floating in thin liquid.
A clear watery border widening around grains.
Creamy without grains or a watery pool at the sides.
quiz.because: Grains and separate liquid signal a loss of the intended continuous texture.

quiz.question: The prepared yogurt splits during hard boiling. What should change?
choices: Heat gently and maintain only a bare simmer.
Boil harder to evaporate the separated liquid.
Add the stabiliser only after a vigorous boil.
quiz.because: Stabilisation does not remove the need for gentle heat; hard boiling can still disrupt the texture.

variant_of.differs: The aim is not body but steadiness: a starch or egg white goes into the cold yogurt first, and the yogurt is stirred one way so that its milk proteins do not clump when it is heated. Thicken stirs a starch into a hot liquid.
